subject.title: Control UI: media/config endpoints 401 over Tailscale Serve origin, breaking local media previews (works fine via loopback)

question: Should verified Tailscale Serve identity be accepted for Control UI HTTP read endpoints, and if so only for config, avatar, and assistant-media reads?
rationale: The bug is source-backed, but the permanent fix decides whether a verified Tailscale identity may cross from the WebSocket Control UI auth surface into HTTP routes that expose config and local media metadata.

options.title: Accept narrow read-route parity
options.body: Review and land the linked PR shape if it limits Tailscale identity to Control UI HTTP reads and proves normal HTTP APIs stay unchanged.

options.title: Keep HTTP token-only
options.body: Update docs/UI behavior so these HTTP reads require explicit shared-secret or device-token credentials even when the WebSocket is accepted by Tailscale identity.

options.title: Fold into proxy auth design
options.body: Defer this to the broader reverse-proxy bootstrap design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12441 before changing endpoint auth.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow read-route parity
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked PR shape if it limits Tailscale identity to Control UI HTTP reads and proves normal HTTP APIs stay unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: He has prior Gateway HTTP/WS auth-boundary history and was the clearest named reviewer in the adjacent reverse-proxy auth design thread.
